findings.issue: The PDP covering predicate filters grants by operation (line 577) and scope-containment (line 585) but does NOT filter by grant.resourceType vs the target's resourceType. Escalation prevention therefore rests ENTIRELY on the disjoint hierarchy node (refToScope's process_instance branch + AncestryOracle returning false for instance-under-record). This is consistent with the pre-existing lattice model (resourceType drives classification/facets, not covering) and is backstopped by the oracle-independent fail-closed kind-guard in fireCardAction, so it is sound — but the single-layer reliance on the AncestryOracle for the scope path is worth a one-line invariant comment so a future oracle change cannot silently re-open the escalation on the PDP layer.
findings.suggestion: Add a comment at grant-resolver.ts:583-589 noting that the covering predicate intentionally does not key on resourceType and that process_instance disjointness is an AncestryOracle invariant (an instance id is never a descendant of any record/registry/application node); the fireCardAction kind-guard is the oracle-independent primary defense.
